pr.title: Restore a dismissed or snoozed inbox item in place
pr.head: b6f59fe62bc1e3d9a0df8e5330c77ca46fe49fcc

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent put a question or a notice in front of the person. The items show in the band, a strip of lines Projector draws above Claude Code's prompt. Each item has a number, and an item opens a drawer of actions when you press its line. The person answers or dismisses a question, and dismisses a notice once read. Either kind can also be snoozed for an hour. When the person answers or dismisses a question, a deliverer sends the agent a line: ANSWER 3.a … or DISMISSED 3 …. The deliverer is the band itself, or project inbox watch in a terminal.

Before this change, a dismissal could not be undone. The agent's only recourse was to ask the question again, which put a duplicate in the band under a new number. A snooze pressed by mistake hid the item at once. This pull request adds a way back:

• project inbox restore <number> reopens a dismissed or snoozed item in place, under the same number and with the same text.
  • The band's drawer offers restore on a dismissed item and unsnooze on a snoozed one. Dismiss and snooze now close the drawer, and the item stays listed, muted, for 30 seconds, which is the window for pressing it again.
  • The mcp__projector__restore tool lets the agent restore an item when the person says a dismissal was a mistake.
  • A new RESTORED 3 … line goes to the agent only when it may already have heard DISMISSED, so it learns the question is open again.

The first review asked for one fix. A restored item did not bring back a band the person had hidden with /projector, although a new question and a snooze that ends both do. The next head fixed that, and its review found the head clean. The latest push applies that review's one suggestion, which moves the restore parser in src/projector/cli.py below snooze's --for option.

cards.title: Terms used on this page
cards.html:
• Band: the lines Projector draws above the prompt, one per pull request or inbox item.
  • Drawer: the actions under an item's line, opened by pressing the line. The band keeps one drawer open at a time, recorded in bandDrawer.
  • Deliverer: whoever sends the agent its line, the band or watch. It claims the line for a token, sends it, and then calls delivered or reopen.
  • restoredAt: set on a restored question whose agent may have heard DISMISSED. It means a RESTORED line is owed.
  • snoozedAt: when an item was last snoozed. The band uses it to keep the item listed for 30 seconds.

cards.title: What the agent hears after a restore
cards.html:
State of the DISMISSED line at the restoreWhat the agent hears
Not yet claimedNothing: the restore cancels the line
Claimed, in flightDISMISSED, then RESTORED
DeliveredRESTORED
A notice, or a snoozeNothing

groups.title: The inbox store learns to restore
groups.kicker: restore, RESTORED, and how dismissal, answer, and delivery treat a restored item
intro: The CLI keeps each item as a JSON file in a per-session store and changes it under the session's lock. A dismissed item has an answer of {dismissed: true}. A dismissed question also gets deliveredAt once its DISMISSED line has gone out, and holds a claim while a deliverer is sending it.

restore removes answer, deliveredAt, and claim from a dismissed item, or snoozedUntil and snoozedAt from a snoozed one. When the agent may have heard DISMISSED, the restore also sets restoredAt, which makes the item owe a RESTORED line. The other changes keep that one owed line correct:

• An answer drops a pending restoredAt and its claim, since ANSWER already tells the agent the question was open.
  • A second dismissal is marked delivered at once when nobody had claimed RESTORED, because the last line the agent heard already said DISMISSED.
  • Settling a claimed RESTORED, as delivered or as reopen, ends it. A failed RESTORED is not retried.
  • A change that lands while a line is in flight drops the line's claim. The deliverer's delivered call then exits 65, and watch now carries on past that error.

checks.text: Ran against a scratch store: a restore while DISMISSED was claimed made the in-flight delivered exit 65, and the next watch --once printed RESTORED 1. Restores of an open item and of a withdrawn item exited 65, and an unknown number exited 66.

files.note: Adds restore and is_restorable, the RESTORED line in message, and the changes to answer, dismiss, snooze, claim, settle, and deliver_pass.

checks.text: A RESTORED line is owed only when DISMISSED was delivered or claimed. A notice never owes one, because dismissing a notice sends nothing.

The second dismissal is marked delivered at once only when restoredAt was set and nobody had claimed it. An expired claim still counts as claimed, so DISMISSED goes out again, which is redundant but harmless.
settle returns before it sets deliveredAt for a RESTORED line, so the question stays open after either outcome.

Without --session, the restore picks the session that holds the number as a dismissed or snoozed item. In a scratch store, session s1 held item 1 open and s2 held item 1 dismissed, and the restore reopened s2's.

files.note: Adds snoozedAt to every item and restoredAt to a question.

groups.title: The CLI command and its permission
groups.kicker: project inbox restore, and why an agent may run it without asking
intro: project inbox restore <number> prints restored 3, or the item with --json. It exits 65 for an item it cannot restore, 66 for an unknown number, and 75 for a busy store, like the other inbox commands.

project init writes permission rules into the person's own host settings. In Claude Code, an ask rule makes an agent get the person's approval before it runs inbox answer, dismiss, or snooze, because those record the person's choice. restore gets no ask rule: it records no answer, and an agent could already put a dismissed question back in front of the person by asking it again. Codex's rules name restore among the allowed inbox commands.

groups.title: The band's drawers and the restore tool
groups.kicker: Restore and unsnooze in the drawer, drawers that close when their line leaves, and the new tool
intro: The band is Projector's hooks module in Claude Code. It reads the store, draws one line per item, delivers lines to the agent, and serves the mcp__projector__* tools. No MCP server runs.

• The drawer. Dismiss and snooze now close the item's drawer. A dismissed item stays listed for 30 seconds after its delivery, struck through. A snoozed item now also stays listed for 30 seconds after snoozedAt, muted but not struck through, and out of the divider's counts. Pressing either line reopens the drawer, where restore replaces dismiss or unsnooze replaces snooze.
  • Drawers that outlive their line. closeLeftDrawer runs on each tick and each reload. It clears the open drawer once its pull request or item is no longer listed. Before, a line that came back reopened with its drawer still open.
  • The restore tool. It runs the CLI and puts the returned item in the band at once. Its description limits it to a dismissal the person calls a mistake.
  • Delivery. needsDelivery counts a pending restoredAt. A failed RESTORED raises its own toast, which does not ask the person to answer again.

checks.text: Ran claude plugin test . at this head: all 111 hook tests passed. hooks/typecheck.sh did not run, because neither this checkout nor the main one has site/node_modules or Claude Code's declarations.

files.note: Adds the restore tool, closeLeftDrawer, the restore and unsnooze actions, the muted line for a snoozed item, the RESTORED toast, and the rule that brings a hidden band back for a restored item.

checks.text: setItems shows a hidden band for any item that is open and not snoozed but that the previous list held as missing, resolved, or snoozed. That covers a new item, and a restore or an unsnooze from a terminal. Checked with a probe test that hides the band and calls the restore tool: at this head the band shows the restored question. The new test a restore brings a hidden band back, from the tool or from a terminal, as a new item does passes.
The tool shows the band itself, because it puts the item in the list before the band reads the store. So when setItems runs, the previous list already holds the item open.

closeLeftDrawer reads the item list against the clock, and the pull request rows against the last snapshot. closeDrawer clears the key only while it is still the open one, so it cannot close a drawer the person opened in the meantime.
Restore keeps the drawer open on the item, while dismiss and snooze close it.
A snoozed item's drawer keeps dismiss and swaps snooze for unsnooze. A dismissed item's drawer shows only discuss and restore.

files.note: Shows a recently snoozed item in isShownAt, counts restoredAt in needsDelivery, and adds the restore tool's description and arguments.

checks.text: isShownAt now returns true for an item snoozed within the last 30 seconds. So setItems and the divider's counts switch to isSnoozedAt, to keep such an item from counting as open.
